solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contract left southern Conservative underfunded

parts.note: 'cut along' is old British slang for leave or go away, so it stands for 'left' as in departed
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
an underfunded project is short of money

explanation.surface: A political complaint: some leftish southern Tory has been starved of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the political wing but the past tense of leaving, which the dated British phrase 'cut along' (be off with you) supplies. The verb definition 'Contract' covers the whole five-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to abbreviate an account, so it is a verbal synonym for shortening or condensing.

clue.text: Curse citation?

parts.note: a curse is a remark made when one is angry, so it is jokingly a mention or citation delivered in a bad temper

explanation.surface: A query about quoting a bad word, perhaps in a dictionary of oaths.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as two words: an irate ('cross') mention ('reference'). The real sense is a pointer from one place in a text to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the term describes an angry mention, which is exactly what swearing at someone amounts to.

clue.text: Cartel concocted case for communications conglomerate

indicators.note: the two words act as a container, a case holding the letters of the answer within them

explanation.surface: A cartel has been cooked up as the legal argument for a big communications firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' looks like an anagram signal but is only fodder; the answer sits across the join of 'Cartel concocted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A telco is the industry's short name for a telephone or telecommunications company, typically a large one.

clue.text: Umpires' equipment encountered during match?

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it, so these letters go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a match is something used to light a fire, a lighter
to have encountered someone is to have met them

explanation.surface: Cricket umpires checking their kit, met in the middle of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' is not the cricket match but the thing you strike to make fire. In cricket, umpires use a light meter to judge whether bad light should stop play.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket umpires carry a device measuring the brightness of daylight to decide if play can continue.

clue.text: Fans welcoming promotion of brilliant tricks with football

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the first word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: enthusiasts or fans are nuts, as in football nuts

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion means moving up, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a brilliant is a cut diamond, so a gem

explanation.surface: Supporters cheering a gifted player promoted for his football skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brilliant' is a noun here, a cut gemstone. A nutmeg is football slang for slipping the ball between an opponent's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmegs are the footballer's trick of passing the ball through an opponent's legs and collecting it beyond.

clue.text: Indirect approach from son showing lethargy

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
lethargy shows itself in idling, doing nothing much

explanation.surface: A father notes his lazy boy's roundabout way of dodging chores.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase, matched by the gerund: a sidling is an approach made sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving furtively sideways towards someone is an oblique, roundabout way of coming near them.

clue.text: Two unknowns performing before one of the Stones

parts.note: a performer on stage is on
y and x are the standard unknown quantities in algebra

explanation.surface: A support act of two nobodies plays before a member of the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Stones' suggests the rock band; it means gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Blyth for one — Chay capsized with broken mast heading north

indicators.note: a capsized boat is overturned and jumbled, so these four letters are rearranged
a broken mast is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged
the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sailor Chay Blyth's boat overturns and its mast breaks on a voyage north.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Chay Blyth is the Scottish sailor who first sailed solo westward round the world; his first name supplies the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Chay Blyth is a famous round-the-world sailor, an example of a man who sails yachts.

clue.text: Interviewee with predictably pedestrian views?

parts.note: the ordinary person stopped by a reporter in a vox pop is literally a pedestrian, and has run-of-the-mill opinions

explanation.surface: A dull interview subject offering the usual dreary opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' does double duty: commonplace views, and the views of someone on foot outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the typical ordinary citizen, the sort quizzed by roving reporters for popular opinion.

clue.text: Bound to be kept in after boil burst

indicators.note: the confinement piece comes after the anagram, so it is placed second
a burst boil breaks open, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: a pupil gated is confined, kept in as punishment

explanation.surface: A teenager must stay at home after a boil bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the anagram before GATED. Gated is British school slang for confined to the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bound to do something means being under a duty or required to do it.

clue.text: 'The Joshua Tree' — carbon copy by half of U2 in a year looking back

indicators.note: looking back faces the reverse way, so the assembled letters are read from right to left
the copy and the band letter are placed inside the two outer letters

parts.note: CC stands for carbon copy, as on a memo

indicators.note: half of the two-character name is its first character

explanation.surface: U2's album 'The Joshua Tree' revisited, a carbon copy from a year back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes U2's 1987 album; the real Joshua tree is a desert plant of the American south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: The Joshua tree is a species of yucca, Yucca brevifolia, found in the Mojave desert.

clue.text: See 1 across
1, 11 or ebb?

definitions.meaning: the combined clue 1, 11 means to abbreviate, to trim down a text
an ebb is a tide going backwards, so the word for tide written backwards; the question mark flags the wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition points to the linked answer at 1 and 11 across, meaning abbreviate. The second is cryptic: an ebb is a tide running back, and TIDE run backwards spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors cut and trim copy, which is shortening a text; the second sense is a tide turned round.

clue.text: Sounds rather like a cute case for haberdashery

indicators.note: the setter tells us the answer, said aloud, is close to the next words

parts.note: cute in the twee, sentimental sense, so a twee, said as 'ay-twee'

explanation.surface: A sewing case is described as having a rather cute sound to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word is pronounced roughly 'ay-twee', which is why 'rather like' softens the match; twee is British for cutesy.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles, thimbles and other sewing items.

clue.text: Android installed with one hands-free program?

indicators.note: the robot has a letter installed in it, placed inside its letters

parts.note: an android is a humanoid robot, an automaton
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Android phone with a hands-free app installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Android' looks like the phone system; it is a robot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanising work so that machines do it without human hands is the point of an automated system.

clue.text: Former Fleet Street newspaper

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Fleet Street in London was home to the British national press, so it stands for the press

explanation.surface: A reference to an old newspaper from London's former press heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the London street where the national papers were based; the Daily Express was one of them, and has since moved away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is a British national tabloid, an example of a daily paper.

clue.text: Circulate with actual pronounced limp too

indicators.note: pronounced means the first word is to be taken as spoken, as a Briton says it, not as spelt

parts.note: proper can mean real or actual, as in a proper job

indicators.note: too means likewise, so the second word is also taken as spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a limp is a way of walking, a gait

explanation.surface: Spreading the word about someone's noticeable limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like it describes a marked limp, but signals that the words are said aloud; 'too' extends that to the second word. Proper gait, said with a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate news or ideas is to spread them widely, to circulate them.

clue.text: Try cocktail of rum and French, as befits a connoisseur

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the spirit are mixed

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: Sampling a rum cocktail and something French, like a true connoisseur.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used adjectivally, as in gourmet food, to fit the definition's 'as befits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmet food or cooking is of the refined standard expected by a discerning epicure.

clue.text: Queen noted for reform may be abrasive

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's royal cipher

indicators.note: something put up for reform is to be reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Queen, a known reformer, may be prickly with her ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abrasive' suggests a person's manner; here it means wearing away, as erosion does.
explanation.definitionFit: An erodent substance or agent wears things away, so it acts like an abrasive.

clue.text: Spooner's 'Shut up, sheep!' revealing camp constraint?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the first letters are exchanged

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut up or confined
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: Spooner shushes a bleating sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: A teg is a dialect word for a young sheep. 'camp constraint' is the peg holding down a tent's guy ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg holds a tent's ropes fast, restraining the shelter at a campsite.

clue.text: Guide's earlier version shows French cheese holding own

indicators.note: the cheese holds the other word within it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A tour guide's first draft features a French cheese with its own character.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Girlguiding movement, Brownies are the younger section before Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls join the junior Brownies section before moving up to become Guides.

clue.text: What 7 may do seeing trouble in fight

indicators.note: the trouble goes inside the fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match, a fight
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sailor in a scrap who spots trouble and gets out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the sailor at 7 down, who bails water out of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor scoops water from a swamped boat with a bucket, emptying it overboard.

clue.text: Test English before ten in the morning

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: An English test scheduled before ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a timetable; 'before ten' is not a time but places E ahead of X.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of a student's knowledge.

clue.text: Regularly say no to one protester

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually turns down offers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: an anti is someone opposed to something, a protester.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who opposes a policy or cause, the kind who demonstrates.

clue.text: Reactionary football management undecided about getting behind

indicators.note: reactionary means going backwards, so the built letters are read right to left
about means around, so the undecided letters wrap around the governing body

parts.note: TBA, to be arranged, marks something not yet decided
the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football

explanation.surface: Conservative football bosses dithering about falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: TBA (to be arranged) is the usual shorthand for undecided. Abaft is a nautical term for towards the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a sailor's word meaning towards the stern, so behind or aft of something.

clue.text: Residents of Okinawa keep alive

indicators.note: residents live inside a place, so the answer lives inside these words

explanation.surface: The people of Okinawa keep themselves alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep alive' looks like one phrase, but 'keep' is fodder and 'alive' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awake means being alert and active, alive to what is going on.

clue.text: Heads of English, Technology, Art, Latin, and the rest

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A list of school department heads, trailing off into all the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of department are the first letters of the subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation means 'and others', used to cut short a list of names.

clue.text: Skill shown by servicemen in extremes of combat

indicators.note: the airmen are placed inside the two outside letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a body of servicemen

explanation.surface: Military skill displayed by soldiers in the thick of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means skill or expertise in an activity, especially a manual one.

clue.text: First-class county perhaps against China next

parts.note: a first-class county cricket team is a professional eleven, a pro XI
in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate

explanation.surface: A county cricket side lines up against China in its next fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' only places the pieces side by side. English first-class cricket is played by county sides, professional elevens; 'china' is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately adjacent, next in order or position.

clue.text: Thin gentlemen spread erudition

indicators.note: spread out letters are moved apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Slender gentlemen are spreading learning about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' reads as a verb of distributing knowledge but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlightenment means insight and learning, the condition of being well informed.
